about.title: Redondo Beach Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Redondo Beach is a compact city by Los Angeles County standards, roughly 68,000 people living between the pier, the Riviera and the neighborhoods that line Artesia Boulevard and Inglewood Avenue. Homes here hold the same everyday items as anywhere else: kitchen appliances, e-bikes, power tools, children's car seats, prescription bottles. When one of those items fails and someone is hurt, California treats the situation differently than an ordinary accident. Under strict product liability, you usually do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. What you need to show is that the product had a defect in its design, its manufacture, or its warnings, and that the defect caused your injury. That distinction changes how a claim is built. Responsibility can also reach past the company whose name is on the box; the distributor and the store that sold it may share liability. LawProactive is a free service that connects Redondo Beach residents with an independent attorney who takes these cases on contingency. We are not a law firm, and you pay us nothing.
about.commonInjuriesTitle: Injuries Commonly Tied to Defective Products
commonInjuries: Burns from overheating lithium batteries in e-bikes, scooters and chargers
Lacerations and amputations from power tools or kitchen equipment
Head and spinal injuries when airbags, seat belts or child seats fail
Choking, poisoning or entrapment from unsafe children's products
Chemical burns and respiratory harm from mislabeled household products
Fractures and crush injuries from collapsing furniture, ladders or fitness gear

whyChoose.title: Why Redondo Beach Residents Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Carelessness
items.desc: California's strict liability rule means the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on whether the maker was negligent. An attorney who knows this framework can build the claim around the defect itself.

items.title: The Product Is the Evidence
items.desc: Whatever failed, from a cracked ladder to a melted charger, should be kept exactly as it is, along with packaging and receipts. The attorneys in our network understand why preserving the item matters before anyone else gets a look at it.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Can Be Held Accountable
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and the retailer that sold you the product may all be liable under California law. That widens the path to recovery, especially when the maker is overseas or hard to reach.

items.question: I was in a crash on Rt 1 in Redondo Beach and I think my airbag or seat belt failed. Is that a product liability case?
items.answer: It can be. Redondo Beach recorded 235 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involve vehicle components that did not perform as designed. If a safety system failed or made your injuries worse, you may have a strict liability claim against the vehicle or part manufacturer in addition to any claim against another driver. Keep the vehicle from being repaired or scrapped until an attorney has had a chance to review it.

items.question: What if I threw away the product or the packaging after I got hurt?
items.answer: It makes the case harder, but not automatically impossible. Photographs, receipts, order confirmations, the model and lot number, and medical records describing the injury can all help show what the product was and how it failed. If you still have any part of it, stop using it and set it aside now. An attorney can advise on what else may be available, such as recall notices or reports from other users.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney who handles product liability claims on contingency, which means you owe no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case. There is no obligation after the first conversation.
